title: Friendship with Armstrong in California in 1954
summary: Alcorn describes Louis visiting him when he worked with Kid Ory in California, and their banter about bands.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: But he was... I could sit on and talk about a little more, man, you know? Because we had so many things in common ourselves, Lou and I.

We were very good friends. I don't know, don't forget in 1954 I went to California. I was working with Kid Ora to hang over. Lou used to come there and play that town, play concert that town. When he'd get off that night he'd come right there. He'd sit down at the ball, stand behind the ball. Sit over there on the side where I'd be playing, you know? Waiting for him to get out and go talk. How you doing? Yeah. Telling me how I would talk.

But he was good friends. He'd start getting a little mixed up with dreams for a long time. Mm-hmm. So he'd waste all this time telling me, You're still crazy about it? He'd say, How come? I'd say, You know what I'm doing? I don't know how you're in the business way. I'm supposed to be out of there. I'd say, Why you sit up there? I'd say, You got some money out there for your band. I got a better band. He'd say, I've got a better band right here. He'd say, Boy, it's a band together. Mm-hmm. I got all individuals. He'd say, But I'd like to make up his mind. And it's a book of them. It's what I'd bring home to Europe. It's a success in Europe. He'd say, They even want over in Europe. He didn't want to go. He didn't go to Europe all these many years. So I went with him in 56. That's when we went to Europe. Boy, he should never been to Europe. I went with him in 56. Why was that? Why did he? Look how young I was under there. Yeah. He should have been to Europe 10 times before I was born. That's how this didn't go nowhere. Hmm. Went to California and he stayed there. Left to California and went to California and I would leave.
Mm-hmm. He never returned to New Orleans. Not to live.
